# Problem

Learners need tutorials that match their goals and current knowledge; instructors need lessons they can assess and reuse in their teaching. Both need clear information about content, prerequisites, difficulty, and duration. They also need evidence that the exercises still work, since a tutorial may remain online after they break or its author stops maintaining it.

The tools used to build a lesson also affect how it runs. learnr runs tutorials as Shiny applications [@learnr]. learnr2 builds on Quarto Live, which uses webR to execute R in the browser [@learnr2; @quartolive]. tutorialverse will give instructors and learners a common way to compare tutorial descriptions and check results across these engines.

## Evidence of need and prior work

Choosing tools for an R tutorial involves practical tradeoffs. Handel's [-@handel2025] comparison of six tools for Quarto exercises shows the hosting, maintenance, and exercise-support decisions tutorial authors face. These differences also affect reuse: instructors need to know a tutorial's requirements and maintenance status before adopting it. tutorialverse will make that information easier to find and compare.

For instructors and learners seeking existing tutorials, discovery presents a related challenge. [rstats-ed](https://github.com/rstudio-education/rstats-ed) addressed it through a community-curated catalog, while acknowledging incomplete coverage. Glittr.org helps users find and compare teaching repositories, but excludes educational-quality evaluation [@vangeest2024]. Consistent descriptions support discovery: TeSS aggregates training metadata, and Bioschemas provides shared specifications for resource descriptions [@garcia2020; @castro2023].

Assessing a resource for reuse requires evidence beyond its description. The Galaxy Training Network combines automated checks with community review and maintenance [@hiltemann2023]. Formal scholarly review serves a different purpose: the [Journal of Open Source Education (JOSE)](https://jose.theoj.org/about) peer-reviews reusable educational materials and software [@joseabout]. tutorialverse will distinguish these external reviews from technical check results.

tutorialverse will bring these practices together across R tutorial engines, linking shared descriptions to validation results, review history, and maintenance information. Existing engines will remain responsible for execution. New engines, browser runtimes, and learning-management systems are outside scope; static hosting will be described and checked as a deployment mode.
